page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no marginal notes printed. Running head top centre, page number top right. Catchword at lower right. Fragments at the far left edge belong to the neighbouring page.

main_text.p: impedimento simus, aut etiã labefactemus, aut deturbemus de cõmunione illa quam imperas, aut ordini tuo aduersentur, aut paci obsista-mus, aut bonum & amœnitatem, quam in com-munione sanctorū posuisti, interuertamus per malitiam, infirmitatem, imprudentiã, aut igno-rationem nostram mente, animo, sermone, aut facto: sed potius quidquid bonum, sanctum, iustum, & cõueniens charitati est, illud virtute Spiritus tui acti cogitemus, studeamus, eloqua-mus, seruemus, faciamusq. ad gloriam tui no-minis: da, ô cælestis Pater, ut te Iehouam co-gnoscamus, & domum tuam in te, quæ spelunca foret sine te; da, ut adeuntes domum tuam, & cõsistentes in ea, sanctissimo zelo agnoscamus, semperque lætemur de iis qui dicunt, & con-silia capiunt de Ecclesia tua adeunda, studio gloriæ tuæ & salutis suæ: da, ut Ecclesia optimè cõstructa sit; & refecta labe illius, quæ hoc tem-pore amplissima est, coagmenta lapides viuos illius pariter: fac, ut omnes ascendant eò ad petcipiendum[?] testimonium verbi salutaris tui, & celebrationem nominis tui exercendam: ef-fice, ô Deus ordinis, ut iustus ordo in misera Christianitate obtineat: ut qui rebus sacris præ-sunt, eas procurent sanctè, abiecta rerum alia-rum omnium cogitatione, & adiecto animo ad salutem gregis illius, quem filius dilectus tuus sanguine pretioso suo comparauit: ut qui rebus ciuilibus & humanis præfecti sunt; suis patri-bus tum in res publicas sibi commissas, tum in

page.notes: Running head and page number as printed. A handwritten "254" in the upper right margin is not printed text and is left out. Fragments at the far left edge are the edge of the neighbouring page and are left out. "petcipiendum" appears to be a printing error for "percipiendum" (the r is missing or damaged); left as printed and marked [?]. Long s is rendered as s throughout; "finus" was read as "simus". Final word "te," is the catchword at lower right.
